cohort: The study included maternal and cord blood samples from PREOBE study participants, comparing those who underwent elective cesarean section with those who had vaginal deliveries.
finding: Elective cesarean section significantly impacted both maternal and cord blood metabolomes compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: In maternal blood, elective CS was associated with lower levels of phospholipids, pyruvic acid, branched chain keto-acids, and other gluconeogenic substrates, while in cord blood, CS was linked to higher Cys levels and lower levels of non-esterified fatty acids, TCA cycle metabolites, gluconeogenic substrates, markers of b-oxidation, and hexoses.
